units.title: The IELTS test at a glance
units.summary: Format and timing of all four sections, Academic vs General Training, paper vs computer, how bands are calculated, and test-day tips.

units.title: Form and note completion
units.summary: Fill in forms and notes from everyday conversations: predict the answer type and listen for corrections.

units.title: Multiple choice
units.summary: Single-answer and choose-TWO questions: paraphrase, rejected options and how to read the options in time.

units.title: Matching
units.summary: Match people, places or days to a list of options while the speaker changes plans.

units.title: Map and plan labelling
units.summary: Follow directions on a map or floor plan: orientation, position language and how to track the speaker.

units.title: Sentence and summary completion
units.summary: Complete sentences and summaries from a lecture: grammar clues, synonyms and word limits.

units.title: Spelling, numbers and dates
units.summary: Letters, phone numbers, postcodes, dates and times — the details that lose easy marks in Part 1.

units.title: Distractors and signposting
units.summary: Recognise corrections, changed plans and the signpost words that tell you where a speaker is going.

units.title: True / False / Not Given
units.summary: Decide whether statements match the facts in a passage — and learn the real difference between FALSE and NOT GIVEN.

units.title: Yes / No / Not Given
units.summary: Identify the writer's opinions and claims in argumentative passages.

units.title: Matching headings
units.summary: Choose the heading that sums up the main idea of each paragraph.

units.title: Matching information
units.summary: Find which paragraph contains a specific piece of information — a skill of fast, careful scanning.

units.title: Matching features
units.summary: Match statements to people, places, dates or categories described in a passage.

units.title: Matching sentence endings
units.summary: Complete sentences by choosing the ending that matches both the meaning and the grammar.

units.title: Multiple choice
units.summary: Single-answer and choose-TWO questions: find the evidence before you look at the options.

units.title: Summary, note, table and flow-chart completion
units.summary: Fill gaps with words from the passage or from a word list, keeping to the word limit.

units.title: Diagram labelling and short-answer questions
units.summary: Label parts of a device or process and answer short questions within the word limit.

units.title: Skimming, scanning and time management
units.summary: Read fast for the gist, find details in seconds and divide your 60 minutes across three sections.

units.title: General Training Reading
units.summary: How the GT Reading paper differs: notices, adverts, workplace documents and one longer text.

units.title: Academic Task 1: the essentials
units.summary: What examiners look for in a Task 1 report, the four-paragraph structure, and how to write a strong overview.

units.title: Academic Task 1: bar charts, pie charts and tables
units.summary: How to describe and compare static and changing data in bar charts, pie charts and tables, with model answers.

units.title: Academic Task 1: processes and maps
units.summary: Describe stages in a process and changes on a map, with sequencing and location language and two model answers.

units.title: Task 1 language: change and comparison
units.summary: Verbs, nouns, adverbs and comparison structures for describing trends and differences accurately.

units.title: General Training Task 1: letters
units.summary: Formal, semi-formal and informal letters: choosing the tone, covering the three bullet points, and useful phrases.

units.title: Task 2: opinion and discussion essays
units.summary: Plan and write 'To what extent do you agree?' and 'Discuss both views' essays with a clear position.

units.title: Task 2: advantages/disadvantages, problem/solution and two-part questions
units.summary: Recognise the remaining Task 2 question types and answer every part of them, with three model essays.

units.title: Paragraphs and cohesion
units.summary: Build clear paragraphs and connect ideas with linking words, reference and substitution — without overdoing it.

units.title: Common grammar errors
units.summary: The mistakes that most often hold writing below Band 7 — with quick corrections.

units.title: Speaking Part 1: introduction and interview
units.summary: Answer everyday questions naturally: extend with a reason and an example, without sounding memorised.

units.title: Speaking Part 2: the long turn
units.summary: Use your one minute of preparation well and keep talking for two minutes with a clear story.

units.title: Speaking Part 3: discussion
units.summary: Give developed, balanced answers to abstract questions — the part that separates Band 6 from Band 7+.

units.title: Fluency and pronunciation
units.summary: Speak smoothly without long pauses, sound natural, and make yourself easy to understand.

units.title: Common topics and question banks
units.summary: Practice questions for all three parts on the topics that come up most often.

units.title: Academic word list highlights
units.summary: High-frequency academic words that appear across Reading passages, Writing Task 2 and Part 3 answers.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: the environment
units.summary: Climate, pollution, energy and conservation words for Writing Task 2 and Speaking Part 3.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: education
units.summary: Schools, universities and learning — words for essays on teaching methods, fees and skills.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: technology
units.summary: Devices, the internet, AI and automation — words to discuss the effects of technology on people and work.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: health
units.summary: Lifestyle, diet, healthcare systems and wellbeing — words for public health essays and personal answers.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: work and careers
units.summary: Jobs, employment, workplaces and the economy — words for Part 1 answers and Task 2 essays about work.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: cities and urban life
units.summary: Housing, transport, planning and community — words for questions about city and country life.

units.title: Topic vocabulary: culture and tradition
units.summary: Heritage, festivals, globalisation and the arts — words for describing your culture and discussing change.

units.title: Collocations
units.summary: Natural word partnerships — the fastest way to sound fluent and raise your Lexical Resource score.

units.title: Paraphrasing techniques
units.summary: Say the same thing in different words — essential for Reading, Listening, Task 1 introductions and Speaking.
